title: What a minstrel show involved
summary: Describes blackface comedians, bands in minstrel shows including Freddy Jenkins and the DeParis brothers, pay, Pullman cars and railroad siding fees.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: [ACCORDING TO CHILTON, THE ENGAGEMENT OCCURRED IN 1927-28, SO MR. MOORE WOULD HAVE BEEN 27]

Oh, I see. So that was the early Twenties. Let's back up some, while we have a little time on the tape. What I'd like to ask you is about the minstrel shows. What went on during a minstrel show? The usual minstrel performance, what did that involve? We talked a little bit before about the End Man, and you had comedy acts and that sort of thing. But what went on in a minstrel show at that time?

Well, they called it "Emmett Till had to stay on his own bottom." That means when you're working in a minstrel show, you've got to be able to take care of your own self and do your work, make the people happy. Because they call it entertainment.
The band had to be very good. They had some good bands in some of them shows. Freddy Jenkins, both the DeParis Brothers, Sidney DeParis -- they used to be on them shows.
Now we're talking about 1915, 1916, around that time?
No. We're talking about after the Greystone Ballroom, headed for New York.

I see. What I meant was that when you were a teenager, these minstrel shows, I was interested in them, since we have only a record of what the minstrel shows were like in the Nineteenth Century. Since you happen to be a person who... Since you worked with a minstrel show, traveled with minstrel shows, like A.G. Allen's Minstrels and the Old Kentucky Minstrels, I was wondering if you would care to talk about minstrel performances, just give us a description of what went on in these things. Did people dress up in outlandish clothing, or did they perform in blackface, burnt cork...?
The comedians did, yes. The comedians were in blackface. But they had the lips painted white. Some of them were painted red.
I see. Did the comedians talk about this? Were they happy about it? Were they disgusted with having to do it...?
Yes. Of course, the money ran small, but everybody seemed to be very happy. The main thing, your room and board didn't cost you nothin', and you had enough money on the outside.
And you traveled by a Pullman car.
Did you have trouble in the towns where...? Did the railroad officials attempt to... Did they treat the band all right, or the...?

No, all they did was just get to bring the Pullman car on the side. You had to expect(?) to pay for the side, you know, when the Pullman car parked, and you'd sit there sometimes, if you wanted to stay there that long, a couple of days.
